PullRequest.Title: Fix cloud customization sync feedback loop
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Fixes a client-customization synchronization feedback loop observed while starting Cloud sessions in the Agents window. Related to microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#9878.

## Findings

A workspace-less Cloud quick chat starts with no customization roots, but after the host reported its scratch working directory (`/root`) the running-session publisher treated that path as a workspace root. Draft and running publishers could therefore alternate customization bundle identities. Failed customization loads were also retried whenever an identical active-client snapshot was republished.

The protocol then repeatedly echoed `session/activeClientSet` and `session/customizationsChanged`. In the original reproduction, one turn produced 702 active-client records and 355 customization-change records, and the loop continued after the response completed.

## Solution

- Keep workspace-less quick chats scoped to an empty customization-root set, even after the host reports a scratch directory.
- Do not automatically retry structurally identical failed customization inputs; retain explicit operation-boundary retries.
- Suppress unchanged running-session publications while session state catches up.
- Deduplicate wire-equivalent active-client publications in the protocol client using canonical serialization, ignoring property order and non-serialized `undefined` fields.

A rebuilt live Cloud run completed successfully with 5 active-client records and 10 customization-change records, with counts stable after completion.

## Validation

- Passed: `npm run build-fast -- --client-only`
- Passed: `npm run typecheck-client`
- Passed: targeted ESLint on all six changed TypeScript files
- Passed: `git diff --check`
- Passed: 5 focused unit tests:
  - protocol active-client deduplication
  - existing-session active-client publication
  - delayed session-state deduplication
  - quick-chat scratch-directory scoping
  - failed customization sync republish behavior
- Passed: live Code OSS Agents-window Cloud session; sent `hello`, received a response, and verified bounded AHP action counts after completion

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: Identical active-client republications retried every failed customization, repeatedly re-reading/re-parsing plugin inputs and emitting protocol updates that fed further active-client publications.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Cloud quick-chat startup could enter a persistent active-client/customization protocol loop; one reproduction produced 702 active-client and 355 customization-change records for a single turn and continued after completion.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: Structurally identical active-client snapshots now reuse the existing sync result instead of re-parsing failed plugins and republishing customization changes; retries remain bounded to explicit operation boundaries via force: true.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: Base line 9412 bypassed the identical-input no-op whenever any prior customization had Error status. Each republished SessionActiveClient assignment reaches CopilotActiveClientHandle.customizations (line 9733), which calls SessionPluginController.sync; sync then invokes pluginManager.syncCustomizations and emits customization state updates. The PR changes the no-op to apply to structurally identical inputs regardless of prior failure, while retryFailedClientSyncIfNeeded explicitly opts into force. The PR's reproduced scenario reports hundreds of active-client/customization records continuing after a turn, matching this call path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a workspace-less Cloud quick chat and publish its active-client customizations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The client resolves the customization scope, then dispatches SessionActiveClientSet across the agent-host protocol; the host assigns the snapshot to CopilotActiveClientHandle, and customization sync must settle before eager create returns when seeded during createChat. The diff removes repeated identical failed-input syncs and keeps quick-chat scope resolution workspace-less.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve, bundle, read, and parse client plugin customizations through AgentCustomizationScope and pluginManager.syncCustomizations
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: After the diff, one sync for each structurally changed client snapshot, plus at most one explicit retry per failed client at an operation boundary; identical active-client echoes reuse the prior result. Quick chats use zero workspace roots, so scratch-directory discovery does not add roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Structurally identical snapshots with any Error result bypassed the no-op and repeated plugin filesystem parsing, while the scratch working directory could create a second scope identity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initial scope resolution and eager create sync are on startup/create critical paths; later explicit retries are on the operation that requested them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch SessionActiveClientSet and receive session/customization actions over the remote agent-host protocol
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One dispatch per changed active-client value while host-confirmed state differs; identical publications are coalesced per session channel and connection.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Repeated active-session syncs compared against cached projected state and could republish while authoritative subscription state lagged, feeding the customization retry loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The initial publication is required for the host to expose client tools/customizations; redundant echoes removed by the diff are not required for progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of active-client republishes, customization entries, workspace roots, and failed client customization sets; effective cardinality is coalesced by structural equality and per-session channel.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Customization syncs for one client are serialized behind client.sync; retryFailedClientSyncIfNeeded first joins outstanding client syncs, then retries failed clients sequentially. Protocol deduplication suppresses concurrent identical publications per channel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Active-client scope is shared by session type and normalized roots while referenced. Workspace-less quick chats now consistently use the empty-root key. Identical customization inputs, including failed results, are negatively cached until an explicit operation-boundary force retry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed equality guards, explicit force retry, scope roots, and protocol dispatch call paths are all directly traced; the PR also provides concrete before/after action counts.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact filesystem parsing duration and customization count vary by installation, but the removed feedback loop and boundary multiplicity are directly evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The diff fixes repeated filesystem/protocol work and preserves bounded explicit retries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Switch among existing agent-host sessions while session state acknowledgement lags
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Selecting a session resolves or reuses its customization scope, reads an existing unmanaged verified subscription in-process, performs structural comparisons, and dispatches only if both verified and last-published values differ.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Initial customization discovery and bundle resolution for a distinct session type/root scope
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most once concurrently for the currently acquired distinct scope; same session type/root identity reuses the active scope, while switching to different roots disposes the prior reference.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same scope-resolution boundary already gated active-client publication; the diff changes only quick-chat roots to empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: scope.whenResolved gates publication for a cold scope; warm resolved scopes proceed without new discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one in-flight-equivalent publication per session channel/connection/value; repeated selection while verified state lags is coalesced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The dispatch boundary existed, but repeated selection could issue the same action while the provider's projected session cache lagged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The first dispatch is required; suppressed identical dispatches are redundant and off the useful critical path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct selected session channels and distinct active-client snapshots after equality coalescing, not every selection event.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each active-session change cancels the prior unresolved dispatch attempt; only the latest selection can pass all identity/token guards. Network dispatch is fire-and-forget but duplicate values are coalesced per channel.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Warm verified subscription state suppresses publication; when verified state is unavailable or delayed, _lastPublishedActiveClients supplies temporary per-channel coalescing. Entries are reset on connection attach and removed on rejection, active-client removal, normal session removal, or a later verified equality check.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for cancellation, comparison, and dispatch cardinality; medium for real-world retained snapshot size.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: A long-lived connection can temporarily retain one snapshot for multiple visited channels, but normal lifecycle cleanup exists and equivalent authoritative session state is already retained for observed sessions; incremental cost is not sufficiently material for a finding.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new map reduces network fan-out; its incremental retention does not meet the materiality threshold.

Scenarios.Scenario: Retry previously failed customizations immediately before an operation
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The operation calls retryFailedClientSyncIfNeeded, waits for outstanding client syncs, identifies failed inputs, then force-runs plugin synchronization before continuing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-read and re-parse the full customization input set for each client with at least one failed input
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full sync per failed client per explicit operation boundary, regardless of the number of failed entries in that client; healthy clients are skipped.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The helper already requested the same full-client retry through sync; the diff adds force:true solely to preserve it after identical passive republishes become no-ops.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The retry is intentionally awaited by the requesting operation and therefore blocks that operation, preserving the pre-diff explicit retry behavior.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of clients with at least one failed customization, after grouping all entries by client.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Outstanding syncs across clients are joined with Promise.all; actual retries then run sequentially across failed clients, and each client's work remains serialized behind its prior sync promise.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Successful and failed identical passive inputs reuse prior results. Failures are retried only when the explicit operation boundary opts out of the negative cache with force:true.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the old condition, changed force option, and serialized retry loop are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Operation frequency and failure prevalence vary, but the diff does not increase retry cardinality relative to the old helper behavior.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. The explicit force preserves necessary retry semantics without restoring the passive feedback loop.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all five changed files and all diff pages. No actionable performance regression was introduced. Recorded the concrete repeated-work regression fix traced to commit 066953e45f645f85d2d33bab8470121d40dfc217.
